test: D4 orientation of the successive phonetic square bridge
question: Does rotating or reflecting one language-side of the phonetic plane improve held-out related-family translation beyond the ordinary orientation?

method.resolutions: 3x3 through 21x21, same continuous primary-feature plane as the existing square-sequence test
method.evidence: Within-family sibling-branch consensus inventories; unrelated script labels are not used.
method.cross_validation: 20 deterministic family-blocked folds. For each resolution, choose one D4 transform using the other 19 folds, then compare it with fixed identity on the held-out fold.
method.score: Harmonic mean of same-cell coverage and (1 - held-out residual-feature loss).
method.control: A deterministic random D4 transform per held-out fold/resolution.
method.support_rule: A resolution replicates only with >=15/20 held-out-fold wins over identity, one-sided sign p<0.05, and positive mean balanced-score delta. A general orientation effect requires replication at >=14/19 resolutions.
method.important_boundary: This tests phonetic-coordinate orientation. It does not by itself test visual writing direction or Hangul/Hanzi layout.

named_language_probe.name: Korean
named_language_probe.status: no same-family PHOIBLE comparator; not scored
